summary:
We developed AstroVitaCS, a web prototype that helps flight surgeons and astronauts monitor crew health on long missions. Each astronaut has a dashboard with vitals (heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature), sleep, mood, hydration, exercise, nutrition and supplement targets, four brain games, box-breathing sessions, and cabin readings (temperature, lighting, noise, radiation). The flight surgeon has a view with a crew overview, alerts, trend charts, and AI analysis for each astronaut, plus a chat to communicate with the crew. All data is simulated.

It addresses the challenge by turning health indicators into readable trends and early alerts, and by supporting prevention in areas NASA identifies as spaceflight risks. NASA Human Research Program pages, JSC-67378, and NASA-STD-3001 guided our indicators and reference ranges. Our additions, such as AI explanations and a fasting-plan idea, are proposals that need medical review, not approved NASA protocols.

It matters because when help from Earth is delayed, noticing health changes early supports crew safety. The AI supports awareness only; flight surgeons remain essential.
details:
​WHAT EXACTLY DOES IT DO?

AstroVitaCS is a web prototype for monitoring crew health on long space missions. It has two views.

Astronaut view: a personal dashboard with vitals (heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, HRV), sleep, mood check-ins, water and exercise logging, meals with calorie, protein, carbohydrate and healthy-fat targets, daily supplement tracking, four brain games, box-breathing sessions, cabin readings (temperature, lighting, noise, CO2, radiation), and a demo fasting plan.

Flight-surgeon view: a crew overview with health status, critical alarms, an analysis page for each astronaut, trend charts with normal ranges, and a chat with the crew.

All data in the prototype is simulated.

​HOW DOES IT WORK?

The backend is written in JavaScript (Node.js) with Express. Data is stored in JSON files, and the frontend is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Readings and logs are compared with reference ranges (for example SpO2 95-100% and heart rate 60-100 BPM) and labelled Normal, In range, or Critical. Out-of-range readings create alerts for the medical team. The "AI Analysis" page uses rule-based logic (if/else rules) over recent history to describe patterns and give a risk level. It does not use an AI model. Astronauts and doctors communicate through a built-in chat. Passwords are hashed with scrypt and sessions use signed tokens. Judges can enter without a password using the "Doctor demo" or "Astronaut demo" buttons. Thresholds are demo thresholds inspired by ACLS/ATLS guidelines and need professional validation.

​AI ANALYSIS MODULE

AstroVitaCS was built with the assistance of Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic. The AI Analysis page is a rule-based decision-support tool, not a machine-learning model.

​HOW DOES IT WORK?

Each vital sign is compared with a reference range and rated normal, warning or critical. Abnormal readings are grouped into a pattern for each astronaut, such as short sleep with high stress. Current values are compared with the astronaut's own 14-day average. The most severe finding sets the risk level: low, moderate or high. "Run AI Analysis" re-evaluates the latest data and logs the run. The same rules drive doctor alerts, the critical alarm and fasting exemptions.

​WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

It puts crew health data in one place, helps astronauts and flight surgeons notice changes early, and supports prevention (sleep, nutrition, hydration, exercise, mental health, cabin environment). This matters when help from Earth is delayed. The analysis supports awareness only. It does not diagnose, and flight surgeons remain essential.

​WHAT DO YOU HOPE TO ACHIEVE?

We hope to grow the prototype with real NASA datasets, wearable sensors, and validation by clinicians, and to add more languages. Longer term, the same approach could support remote or isolated communities on Earth. Our additions, including the fasting-plan idea, are proposals, not approved NASA protocols.

​LIMITATIONS

All thresholds are fictional demo values. They need medical approval before any real use. Results are advisory only. They are not diagnoses, and the system does not prescribe treatment. All data is fictional.

​TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, SOFTWARE

​Backend: JavaScript (Node.js 22+), Express 5, cors; JSON file storage (no database); Node built-in crypto module (scrypt for password hashing, HMAC-SHA256 for signed tokens).

​Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript.

​Hosting: GitHub Pages (frontend).

​Presentation: Gamma.

​AI assistance used: Claude and ChatGPT helped write code; Claude helped write each frontend file; AI-generated images in the slides are labelled.

​Hardware: none (software only, simulated data).

​References: NASA Human Research Program risk pages, NASA JSC-67378, NASA Human Adaptation to Spaceflight, NASA-STD-3001, NIH Office of Dietary Supplements.
